references.text: Direct fulfillment of the prayer's sign: The servant's expectation (v.14) meets Rebekkah's action (v.46).
Complementary part of the same prayer: The criterion for confirmation (v.44) is identical to the content of the prayer (v.14).
Narrative precursor: The introduction to the situation of the prayer (v.43) before the specific condition (v.14) is stated.
Theological parallel: Divine guidance through specific criteria to identify the chosen one (king/bride).
Narrative conclusion: Confirmation that Rebekkah is the chosen one after the sign was given.
Direct reference: The servant demands an answer based on the condition he asked for in v.14.
Direct fulfillment: The servant sees Rebekkah coming exactly as he asked in v.14.
